theory: Question 12, lines 400–406, teaches estimating by rounding each number to 1 significant figure. Explain that general method, including rounding both factors when necessary; retaining a one-digit whole-number factor is a valid special case. The supplied booklet does not teach upper/lower product estimates, bracketing or above/below classification as assessed tasks, so remove their presentation as required procedures and keep dependent solutions consistent.
summary: Replaced unsupported upper/lower estimates and bracketing tasks with product-estimation questions using new values, and repaired benchmark-selection and classification demands while preserving supported calculations, quiz ids and mastery designations. Updated theory and affected worked examples to teach rounding each factor to 1 significant figure, corrected task slugs and supplied booklet citations for every practice and quiz item; no whole items were removed.
reviewSummary: All supplied items have correct answers and use the product-estimation question type explicitly asked in booklet Question 12(a–b), with equivalent place-value rounding where specified. The theory and worked examples are consistent with the taught method, every quiz has exactly one correct option with accurate distractor explanations, and no removals or repairs are required.
